summary.headline: Honasa Q2 FY27: management calls it the highest-growth quarter since IPO, with EBITDA margin of 12.7% and about 100 bps of EBITDA gain from channel and category mix.
summary.overview: Management described Q2 FY27 as the highest-growth quarter since the company listed, with a 12.7% EBITDA margin despite gross margin near 70%. Management attributed roughly 100 bps of EBITDA improvement to channel mix (offline, quick commerce, B2B) and better advertising efficiency across Mamaearth, Dermaco and younger brands. Growth was driven by focus categories (face wash, shampoo, sunscreen, moisturisers, hair colour and styling), with younger brands ex-Dermaco growing about 40-45%. Management reiterated a medium-term EBITDA margin ambition but declined to give quarter-on-quarter growth or margin percentages for Q3.

financial_highlights.change: Management says about 100 bps of EBITDA improvement came from channel and ad efficiency; prior-year comparison not stated

financial_highlights.value: Highest growth quarter since IPO (per management, over last 12 quarters)

financial_highlights.change: Analysts' questions cited 40% and 45%; management said 40%+ in one answer and 45% in another

financial_highlights.value: High-teens growth stated as 'high teens' in Q&A (exact figure unclear in transcript)
financial_highlights.change: Analyst referred to a higher base versus H2 and asked whether high teens or mid teens can hold

segments.name: Mamaearth
segments.commentary: Management said growth is strong online and offline; Nielsen-measured face wash share is about 1.2%, with outlets rising to about 65,000 and a stated 300,000 reference point. Face wash share gained 140 bps and shampoo share gained 50 bps, per management.

segments.name: Younger brands (ex-Dermaco)
segments.commentary: Growing about 40-45%, with D2C growth not captured in the offline channel figures. Management did not give a sales share for the segment.

segments.name: Dermaco
segments.commentary: Management did not give Dermaco growth or sales in the call. Its offline growth is cited as a driver of the offline mix shift.

segments.name: Bblunt
segments.commentary: Hair colour portfolio growing 100%+, with styling growing on quick commerce. Shampoo and conditioner is described as 'doing okay' and is being relaunched.

segments.name: Dr. Sheth
segments.commentary: Brand proposition is being revisited because consumers are shifting toward active products; higher-age actives such as Botox and collagen ranges are performing well.

segments.name: Aqualogica
segments.commentary: Management is expanding into body care and moisturisers and reports improving Gen Z acceptance.

guidance_outlook: Medium-term target: EBITDA margin growth to about 13% (per management, 'next four years'), with an overall aim of about 15%, and a longer-term ambition of around 50% in the analyst's framing.
Management declined to give a Q3 sequential growth percentage but said Q3 will be higher than Q2.
Management said it has no year-wise margin target; some years may see only 50-70 bps of expansion if the company doubles down on growth.
Guidance for 150-200 bps margin improvement this year was discussed; management said it was not being aggressive or conservative and sees current levels as comfortable.
capex_capacity: No capacity, capex or commissioning figures were discussed in the call.
demand_pricing: Focus category market is about INR 50,000 crore and the company holds about 5% share; management sees large headroom.
Hair colour penetration in India is about 5%+ in the dye segment, and the category is shifting toward creme, toxin-free and non-black shades.
Price increases (MRP) were a driver of value growth, with volume growth lagging value growth.
Face wash is the largest and fastest-growing category, followed by shampoo, sunscreen and moisturisers, each growing 20%+ in the quarter.
Per-capita beauty spend in India is among the lowest in Asia; management expects strong category growth over the next decade.

qa_highlights.question: Growth of younger brands excluding Dermaco, and what drives it given that the offline and online channel figures appear constrained?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said younger brands ex-Dermaco are growing 40%+; D2C growth is not captured in the offline/modern trade figures cited.

qa_highlights.question: What gives confidence Mamaearth can sustain high-teens or mid-teens growth on a higher base?
qa_highlights.answer: Growth is coming equally from online and offline, with e-commerce also growing in high teens; 80% of growth comes from current stores, and Nielsen inventory turns have improved.

qa_highlights.question: Which focus categories are driving the 350-400 bps contribution gain?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said face wash, shampoo, sunscreen and moisturisers all grew 20%+; face wash is the largest and fastest-growing category.

qa_highlights.question: Is the margin improvement from lower third-party platform commissions as channel mix shifts to B2B, quick commerce and offline, and is the 150-200 bps guidance conservative?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said part of the margin improvement is from channel mix; it said it is not being aggressive or conservative and sees current levels as comfortable.

qa_highlights.question: Will volume and value growth divergence reverse as offline grows faster?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the gap mainly to MRP increases and pack/brand mix. It does not expect a major mix shift to offline; e-commerce and offline are both expected to grow strongly.

qa_highlights.question: Can sequential Q3 growth of about 10-12% be sustained after a high Q2 base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q3 will be higher than Q2 but would not give percentages, and it does not expect sequential growth to follow the prior pattern.

qa_highlights.question: Hair colour entry and Bblunt performance?
qa_highlights.answer: Bblunt hair colour is growing 100%+; management is considering entry into hair colour through another brand and will announce it when launched.

risks_watch: Growth is concentrated in price-led value growth; volume growth is lagging value, so management's price-led growth must be tested in Q3.
Margin expansion depends on channel mix and ad efficiency; the company's own guidance and the 13%/15% medium-term targets are not tied to specific years.
Dermaco's growth and sales were not disclosed, which limits visibility into the younger-brand segment's contribution.
Mamaearth's growth is expected to slow on a higher base; management did not give a precise figure.
Shampoo and conditioner is being relaunched, and Dr. Sheth's proposition is being revisited, which could create execution risk in those brands.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and category headroom, with management describing the quarter as its best since listing. Cautious on specifics: it declined to give Q3 quarter-on-quarter percentages and did not give precise Dermaco or Mamaearth growth figures.
key_quotes: FY 27 is the highest growth quarter since we have gone public in the last 12 quarters.
So a lot more headroom to grow just by focusing on focus categories and continuing to minimize and handshare is what we can see happening over the next few five years.
Of course Q3 will be higher than Q2 but we wouldn't be able to comment on percentages
I have not seen any benefits of bringing to aggressive conservative probably the better ways to be

growth.why: Management called Q2 FY27 the highest-growth quarter since IPO, with younger brands ex-Dermaco growing 40-45% and Q3 guided to be higher than Q2, but gave no revenue growth percentage, no capacity additions, and reiterated the 150-200 bps FY27 margin expansion without restating numbers; backing is mainly pricing, mix and share gains with no capex or order detail.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management reiterated 150-200 bps FY27 EBITDA margin expansion and a ~13% medium-term target, and attributed ~100 bps of the EBITDA gain to channel mix and ad efficiency, though it warned some years may add only 50-70 bps.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No capacity, plant or commissioning figures were discussed in the call.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Growth is mainly price-led (MRP increases) with volume lagging value, and face wash, shampoo, sunscreen and moisturisers each grew 20%+, so volume recovery is conditional and unproven.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex was not discussed and no utilisation figure was given.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management called current margin levels comfortable and said it is neither aggressive nor conservative on the 150-200 bps guide, so no upgrade was signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Mamaearth growth is expected to slow from high teens on a higher base, and management gave no Q3 sequential percentage, so the growth trajectory is unconfirmed.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management is considering a hair colour entry through another brand, to be announced at launch, and Shampoo/conditioner is being relaunched and Dr. Sheth's proposition revisited.

rows.label: Price-led value growth from MRP increases
rows.why: MRP increases drove value growth while volume lagged, so sustaining value growth depends on pricing holding into Q3.

rows.label: Modern trade offtake growth 40%+ and offline/B2B channel expansion
rows.why: Modern trade offtake grew 40%+ and channel mix (offline, quick commerce, B2B) contributed ~100 bps of EBITDA gain, with management expecting strong offline and e-commerce growth.

rows.label: Bblunt hair colour growth 100%+
rows.why: Bblunt hair colour is growing 100%+ and hair colour penetration is only about 5%+ in the dye segment, leaving headroom for continued share gains.

tone.note: Management was confident on the highest-growth quarter since IPO, category headroom (INR 50,000 crore, ~5% share) and channel mix margin gains, but cautious on specifics: no Q3 sequential percentage, no precise Dermaco or Mamaearth growth. Analysts pushed on whether high-teens Mamaearth growth holds
